CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie is a 49-year-old female with past medical history significant for congestive heart failure, kidney stones, and prior colonoscopy who presents today with an abnormal lab finding of low hemoglobin. Patient reports over the past couple of months she has been really tired and dizzy. She has been worn out and getting tired from activities such as walking a mile or going to work, which previously did not cause her to tire. She denies blood in stools currently, though she did have blood in stools about three years ago which prompted a colonoscopy. She denies dark, tarry, or black stools. She denies heavy menstrual bleeding. She denies passing out though she has felt a bit dizzy. She denies weight loss or loss of appetite. Regarding her congestive heart failure, patient notes that watching her salt intake has been more of a struggle recently. She has been traveling to Vermont and has stopped at McDonald's where she consumed two cheeseburgers. She has noticed some swelling in her legs but states it is not extreme. She denies shortness of breath or problems lying flat at night. Regarding her kidney stones, she denies recent flare-ups, back pain, flank pain, or blood in urine. She reports having some nasal congestion due to seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
As noted above, patient endorses dizziness, fatigue, leg swelling, and seasonal nasal congestion. She denies fever, chills, sore throat, cough, weight loss, loss of appetite, syncope, blood in stools, dark stools, heavy menstrual bleeding, shortness of breath, orthopnea, back pain, flank pain, and hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, kidney stones, prior colonoscopy with findings of mild diverticulosis approximately three years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 milligrams daily
Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily
Lasix 40 milligrams once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently traveled to Vermont. Works at a job requiring physical activity.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs within normal limits. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Cardiovascular exam: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted (previously heard). Lower extremities: trace to 1+ pitting edema in bilateral ankles.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin: 8.2 (low)
Echocardiogram from approximately six months ago: Left ventricular ejection fraction approximately 45% with moderate mitral regurgitation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. New anemia: Order anemia profile labs to determine type of anemia. Refer to gastroenterology for evaluation with probable endoscopy and colonoscopy.
2. Congestive heart failure: Fluid retention noted. Start Lasix 40 milligrams once daily. Continue Toprol 50 milligrams daily. Continue Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Patient instructed to watch salt intake closely, weigh herself daily, and call if weight increases, as may need to increase diuretic dose.
3. Kidney stones: Continue to watch diet and stay hydrated. Call with any questions or concerns.
